about: Nuclides for FY14 Road to Fusion. Masses are atomic masses (neutral atoms, electrons included) from AME2020, apart from the free proton (CODATA 2018). Binding energy per nucleon is the AME2020 value (B/A, from the atomic masses with the electrons' binding neglected), checked here against B = (Z m(1H) + N m_n - m) c^2 to 0.002 MeV. Stability and half-lives from NUBASE2020; 'stable' means no decay has been observed.

nuclides.name: neutron
nuclides.note: A free neutron decays (mean lifetime about 880 s); inside a stable nucleus it does not.

nuclides.name: proton
nuclides.note: A free proton; the hydrogen-1 atom is a proton plus an electron.

nuclides.name: bismuth-209
nuclides.note: Radioactive, but the half-life is about a billion times the age of the Universe: for most purposes stable.

reactions.label: Tritium breeding: lithium-6 + neutron → helium-4 + tritium
Fission: uranium-235 + neutron → barium-141 + krypton-92 + 3 neutrons

long_lived_note: long_lived: half-life of 500 million years or more, so still found in nature (primordial).
chart_note: Every ground-state nuclide with Z up to 94 that NUBASE2020 lists with a measured half-life or as stable, keyed 'Z-N'.

energy_scales.note: Energy released by one reaction (or molecule) and per kilogram of fuel. Chemical fuels: higher heating values. Values computed from the numbers here; the sources say where the inputs come from.

items.label: Burning methane
items.how: Both values use the higher heating value (the water formed is condensed), as for coal. Per molecule: $890.7\ \text{kJ/mol} : (6.022 \cdot 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}) = 1.479 \cdot 10^{-18}\ \text{J} = 9.23\ \text{eV}$ per molecule of $\text{CH}_4$. Per kilogram: $55.5\ \text{MJ/kg}$ of methane (the oxygen from the air is not counted).
items.source: Wikipedia, Heat of combustion (table: methane HHV 55.52 MJ/kg, LHV 50.00 MJ/kg, 890.7 kJ/mol), checked 2026-11-01

items.label: Burning coal
items.how: Anthracite, higher heating value $32.5\ \text{MJ/kg}$ (other coals give less, about $15$–$30\ \text{MJ/kg}$).
items.source: Wikipedia, Heat of combustion (table: anthracite HHV 32.50 MJ/kg), checked 2026-11-01

items.label: U-235 fission
items.how: About $200\ \text{MeV}$ recoverable per fission. One kilogram of $^{235}\text{U}$ contains $1\ \text{kg} : (235.04\ \text{u} \cdot 1.66 \cdot 10^{-27}\ \text{kg/u}) = 2.56 \cdot 10^{24}$ nuclei, so $E = 8.21 \cdot 10^{13}\ \text{J}$.
items.source: Wikipedia, Nuclear fission (about 200 MeV recoverable of 207 MeV per U-235 fission), checked 2026-11-01; mass of U-235 from AME2020

items.label: D–T fusion
items.how: $Q = 17.6\ \text{MeV}$ from the AME2020 masses; one reaction uses $5.030\ \text{u}$ of fuel (one deuterium and one tritium atom). Per kilogram: $E = 17.6\ \text{MeV} \cdot 1.602 \cdot 10^{-13}\ \text{J/MeV} : (5.030\ \text{u} \cdot 1.661 \cdot 10^{-27}\ \text{kg/u}) = 3.37 \cdot 10^{14}\ \text{J}$.
items.source: Computed from AME2020 atomic masses and CODATA 2018 constants (this file)
